meta.title: Grupo de Puebla — Cronologia
meta.subtitle: Chronology of the Grupo de Puebla — the Latin American progressive forum of individuals (2019–present)
meta.description: An open, source-referenced chronology of the Grupo de Puebla, the forum of Latin American (and southern-European) progressive leaders founded in Puebla, Mexico, in July 2019: its encuentros, declarations, CLAJUD, and its constantly conflated — but institutionally separate — relationship to the Foro de São Paulo.
meta.dataQualityNote: Work-in-progress dataset on a young, politically contested organization. Official grupodepuebla.org pages are volatile (the site has already been reorganized) and are archived where possible; the 'renamed Foro de São Paulo' narrative comes from opinion journalism and is presented as an attributed claim, rebutted with the documented coexistence of both organizations; membership lists fluctuate and are dated. Corrections against primary sources are welcome.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A forum of progressive INDIVIDUALS — presidents, ex-presidents, ministers, legislators, academics — from Ibero-America, founded in Puebla, Mexico, in July 2019; no formal treaty headquarters, coordinated by an executive coordinator with support foundations.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: 12–14 July 2019, Puebla, Mexico, at the 'Encuentro Latinoamericano ProgresivaMente'; the Declaración de Puebla (14 July) constituted the 'Grupo Progresista Latinoamericano', quickly known as Grupo de Puebla.

facts.label: Coordination
facts.value: Marco Enríquez-Ominami (Chile) is executive coordinator and the group's public face, with co-coordinators including Ernesto Samper; operational support from Fundación Progresa (Chile) and Corporación Escenarios (Colombia).

facts.label: Key distinction
facts.value: NOT the Foro de São Paulo renamed: the FSP (1990, São Paulo) is a forum of PARTIES; the Grupo de Puebla (2019) is a forum of individuals — both exist today and met separately, simultaneously, in Tegucigalpa in June 2024.

facts.label: Signature causes
facts.value: The anti-'lawfare' agenda (CLAJUD, launched January 2020 under Baltasar Garzón), Lula's freedom (2019), the Bolivia 2019 'golpe' statement, Assange's release, and successive declarations against the regional right.

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: Founded by ~30 leaders from about 12 countries; the current official founders list claims around 64 members from 18+ countries — the list fluctuates and is dated as retrieved.

events.title: I Encuentro — founding
events.text: Over 30 leaders from about 12 countries meet at the 'Encuentro Latinoamericano ProgresivaMente', driven by Marco Enríquez-Ominami with Alberto Fernández, Ernesto Samper and Aloizio Mercadante; the Declaración de Puebla (14 July) constitutes the group, with founding statements on progressive dialogue, 'lawfare' and Venezuela. López Obrador never joined: Morena was represented by its president Yeidckol Polevnsky — the 'AMLO patronage' framing belongs to critical outlets and is attributed.

events.title: II Encuentro — 'El cambio es el progresismo'
events.text: 32 leaders from 12 countries, hosted by president-elect Alberto Fernández; opened with a video message from Lula, freed from prison on 8 November: 'Estoy libre y con muchas ganas de pelear'.

events.title: Bolivia: the 'golpe' statement
events.text: From Buenos Aires the group declares Evo Morales's ouster 'un golpe de estado', demands the interim government return power, and condemns 'arbitrary persecution of progressive leaders'.

events.title: CLAJUD launched
events.text: The Consejo Latinoamericano de Justicia y Democracia — agreed at the founding meeting per the official site — is publicly launched under ex-judge Baltasar Garzón to study 'lawfare' and human-rights cases; members include Carol Proner and Adoración Guamán, with E. Raúl Zaffaroni contributing to its publications.

events.title: The pandemic encuentros (III–VI)
events.text: Four virtual encuentros with 30–60 leaders (per ES Wikipedia): 'Puebla–Chile' with the declaration 'En tiempos de pandemia, unidad en las propuestas', 'Puebla–Colombia', and the first-anniversary encuentro of July 2020.

events.title: The Manifiesto Progresista
events.text: A 33-point manifesto proposes a 'modelo solidario de desarrollo' as the alternative to neoliberalism; presentation dated 11 February by Cubadebate/teleSUR and 18 February by others — the divergence is recorded against the official PDF.

events.title: VII Encuentro
events.text: About 200 leaders from 19 countries; members publicly endorse Gabriel Boric ahead of Chile's 19 December runoff.

events.title: The Assange letter
events.text: The group and CLAJUD — with signatures including Lula, Dilma Rousseff, Samper and Lugo — demand Julian Assange's freedom after the Westminster extradition ruling; later statements after his 2024 release credited Correa's asylum decision.

events.title: VIII Encuentro
events.text: About 150 leaders from 18 countries meet in newly Petro-governed Colombia; President Boric — not a member — sends a video greeting: 'Nos necesitamos más unidos que nunca'.

events.title: IX Encuentro
events.text: About 200 leaders from ~21 countries return to Puebla — in person Samper, Evo Morales, Correa, Zelaya, Leonel Fernández and Zapatero; virtually Lula, Mujica, Dilma and Alberto Fernández. The declaration warns of 'una derecha antidemocrática... con ideología fascista'. Dates diverge: 30 Sep–1 Oct (official/SELA) vs 1–3 Oct (ES Wikipedia) — recorded.

events.title: The Milei era opens
events.text: After Javier Milei takes office the group calls his mega-decree 'un atropello al sistema republicano'; Milei's allies (Fundación Disenso) had cast him as 'the alternative to the Grupo de Puebla and the Foro de São Paulo' — a useful specimen of how right-wing discourse conflates the two organizations.

events.title: 'Ocúpese de lo importante'
events.text: After Milei mocks the group, it replies with the statement 'Ocúpese de lo importante'.

events.title: The Zúñiga coup attempt
events.text: The group repudiates the attempted coup in Bolivia; the Bolivian government's pushback to the statement is reported — single-source, flagged.

events.title: X Encuentro — and the coexistence proof
events.text: Hosted by President Xiomara Castro on the 15th anniversary of the 2009 coup against Zelaya; declaration 'Renovar el progresismo para relanzar la esperanza' and a call for a 'plan de acción para frenar el neofascismo'. Crucially for disambiguation: the Foro de São Paulo, the Grupo de Puebla, the Progressive International and CELAC Social all met the same week in Tegucigalpa as separate organizations.

events.title: The Venezuela election controversy
events.text: The group's statement on the 28 July 2024 election — 'monitoring the process, no external interference' — draws criticism including from within its own orbit; Emol titles it 'El complicado momento del Grupo de Puebla'.

events.title: Alberto Fernández suspended
events.text: The co-founder's participation is suspended ('at his request') after Fabiola Yáñez's gender-violence complaint (filed 6 August 2024); right-leaning outlets criticize the group for not expelling him outright — attributed.

events.title: Defense of Evo Morales
events.text: Statements of concern over a 'lawfare campaign' against Morales (4 October) and rejection of the alleged assassination attempt against him (27 October).

events.title: Five-year self-assessment
events.text: The group publishes its anniversary balance '5 años impulsando el cambio en Iberoamérica'.

events.title: Death of Pepe Mujica
events.text: José 'Pepe' Mujica, member and moral reference of the group, dies at 89; the group's tribute: 'despide al hombre que sirvió sin privilegios'.

events.title: 'Democracia Siempre' — not a GdP event
events.text: The summit of sitting presidents (Lula, Boric, Petro, Sánchez, Orsi) is a presidents' initiative that the Grupo de Puebla merely endorsed (statement of 24 July 2025) — included to prevent conflation.

events.title: Joint statement with the Progressive International
events.text: The Grupo de Puebla and the Progressive International jointly condemn the US 'economic war' on Venezuela, signed by leaders from ~20 countries — confirming the two are distinct organizations that co-sign.

events.title: 2026 activity
events.text: From the official comunicados page (retrieved July 2026): statements on Bolivia's crisis (May), celebration of member Iván Cepeda reaching Colombia's presidential runoff (31 May), a virtual meeting of leaders from 23 countries (June), and a lawfare statement regarding Spain (July). No XI Encuentro has been held as of July 2026 — the official index still ends at Tegucigalpa.

figures.name: Marco Enríquez-Ominami
figures.role: Chilean ex-presidential candidate; founder and executive coordinator — the group's public face; his Fundación Progresa provides operational support.

figures.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
figures.role: Member; his November 2019 release from prison was the group's first emblematic cause; president of Brazil since 2023.

figures.name: Ernesto Samper
figures.role: Colombian ex-president; founder and co-coordinator; his Corporación Escenarios is one of the group's support institutions.

figures.name: Alberto Fernández
figures.role: Argentine ex-president; co-founder and host of the II Encuentro; participation suspended in August 2024 after a gender-violence complaint (the complaint is attributed; the suspension is the group's own act).

figures.name: Dilma Rousseff, Rafael Correa and Evo Morales
figures.role: Ex-presidents of Brazil, Ecuador and Bolivia; members — Morales at the center of the group's Bolivia statements of 2019 and 2024.

figures.name: José 'Pepe' Mujica
figures.role: Uruguayan ex-president; member and moral reference; died 13 May 2025 at 89.

figures.name: José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero
figures.role: Spanish ex-prime minister; member — the group's southern-European extension.

figures.name: Baltasar Garzón
figures.role: Spanish ex-judge; head of CLAJUD since its January 2020 launch.

figures.name: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas
figures.role: Mexican founding member; press reports of his later distancing are flagged for verification.

figures.name: Irene Montero
figures.role: Spanish MEP and ex-equality minister; listed on the current official members page — whether she was a 2019 founding signatory is unverified and flagged.

figures.name: Gabriel Boric
figures.role: NOT a member: Chile's president has repeatedly sent greetings to encuentros and named Chile's participants, but does not appear on the member list — recorded to prevent a common conflation.

organizations.name: Grupo de Puebla (structure)
organizations.relation: A forum of individuals with no formal treaty headquarters: executive coordinator (Enríquez-Ominami) plus co-coordinators, supported by Fundación Progresa (Chile) and Corporación Escenarios (Colombia); sub-structures include CLAJUD, a parliamentary group and the CESP study center (the latter two per ES Wikipedia).

organizations.name: CLAJUD
organizations.relation: The Consejo Latinoamericano de Justicia y Democracia: the group's anti-'lawfare' legal council of ~20 jurists under Baltasar Garzón, with Carol Proner and Adoración Guamán; agreed at the July 2019 founding per the official site, publicly launched January 2020 — both dates stated.

organizations.name: Foro de São Paulo
organizations.relation: The 1990 São Paulo forum of PARTIES — distinct from and coexisting with the Grupo de Puebla; the two met separately, simultaneously, in Tegucigalpa in June 2024. Documented in the sibling fsp project.

organizations.name: Progressive International
organizations.relation: The global left international launched by DiEM25 and the Sanders Institute — organizationally distinct; the two co-sign statements (Venezuela, December 2025) and coincided in Tegucigalpa 2024.

disambiguation.note: The group's name invites systematic conflations — these cards are the project's core service.

items.title: Grupo de Puebla ≠ Foro de São Paulo
items.text: FSP: founded 1990 in São Paulo, by PARTIES (including the Cuban CP). Grupo de Puebla: founded 2019 in Puebla, by INDIVIDUALS. Both are active today and met separately, simultaneously, in Tegucigalpa in June 2024 — the cleanest single proof against the 'renaming' myth, which comes from opinion journalism (Diario Las Américas, ADN América, Infobae opinion) and is presented here as an attributed claim. Overlap of individuals (Lula's orbit) explains, but does not justify, the conflation.

items.title: ≠ the Puebla Conference of 1979
items.text: CELAM's III General Conference (Puebla, January–February 1979, opened by John Paul II) shares only the city's name — zero relation; that event is documented in the sibling celam project.

items.title: ≠ the Progressive International
items.text: A distinct global organization (DiEM25/Sanders Institute, launched 2020) with movement-based membership; the Grupo de Puebla is an Ibero-American forum of individuals. They co-sign statements — which requires them to be different things.

items.title: ≠ the 'Democracia Siempre' summit
items.text: The July 2025 Santiago summit was an initiative of sitting presidents that the group merely endorsed.

items.title: The founding name
items.text: Constituted as 'Grupo Progresista Latinoamericano' at an event called 'ProgresivaMente'; the media consolidated 'Grupo de Puebla'.
